explanation: In Russia, showing the soles of your feet is considered disrespectful because the foot is seen as the lowest and dirtiest part of the body. This gesture can be interpreted as a sign of contempt or disregard, especially in social settings where mutual respect is expected.
local_tip: Always keep your feet flat on the floor or crossed at the ankles, and avoid pointing the sole of your shoe or foot toward anyone.
regional_note: This norm is consistent across most of Russia, though younger generations in urban areas may be slightly more relaxed about it in informal settings.

also_check.note: The foot is considered the lowest part of the body, and pointing the sole at someone is a grave insult.
Showing the soles of your feet is generally not offensive, though it may be seen as casual or relaxed.
Showing the sole of your foot to someone is highly disrespectful, as the foot is considered unclean.
